newsitem.title: FRANCE: France creates task force to fight EU budget fraud.
newsitem.headline: France creates task force to fight EU budget fraud.

text.p: The French government stepped up the fight against fraudulent use of European Union funds with the establishment on Wednesday of a special domestic task force.

"Fraud is unacceptable in all its forms but I think fraud in the Community budget provokes particular resentment from our citizens," European Affairs Minister Michel Barnier said as he announced the creation of the anti-fraud task force ICLAF.

He said the European Commission's 1995 annual report estimated that around 1.1 billion European currency units, or nearly 1.5 percent of its budget, had been wrongly diverted. "That's a lot," Barnier said.
The Commission in 1994 declared the fight against fraud a priority and created the UCLAF anti-fraud coordination force.
The new French task force will monitor the activities of French agencies involved in fighting fraud and will be France's link with the UCLAF, Budget Minister Alain Lamassoure said.
Given the budgetary rigour of European governments straining to meet the Maastricht criteria for monetary union, the campaign to stamp out fraud at EU level is more important than ever, he said.

"Over the past three years, the total amount of fraud and irregularities detected by the Commission and member states has grown more than fivefold, rising from 204 million Ecus in 1992 to more than 1.1 billion in 1995," he said. He said the rise reflected the success of the anti-fraud campaign.
Lamassoure said France contributes 18 percent of the EU budget, while around 16 percent is spent in France.
